ecdysterone induces a group of small heat-shock genes and proteins in both cultured cells and imaginal disc tissues.
ecdysterone induces four small heat-shocks genes in Drosophilia S3 cells and in imaginal discs.
the ecdysterone-induced synthesis and accumulation of the four small heat-shocks proteins in the Drosophila imaginal disc and S3 cell is accompanied by a corresponding accumulation of their mRNA.

the induction of the small hsp genes by ecdysteroids in Drosophilla.
the induction of heat shock proteins in Drosophilla.
the regulation of gene expression by ecdysone.

ecdysterone is a potent inducer of four small heatshock proteins in both S3 cells and in vivo, and that this induction occurs in both the absence and presence of high temperature.

the ecdysteroids are the primary regulators of the synthesis of four heat-shocked proteins in Drosophilla cells.

ecdysterone is a hormone which can induce the transcription of small hsp genes.
